unit.title: Loop engineering
unit.moc: eval harness — instrumented gates & the seam — skills compounding — Multica: evaluate AND integrate — re-platform triggers

checkpoint.title: Checkpoint 4 — gate
checkpoint.prompt: Order the top layers (eval harness before skills compounding) and name the re-platform triggers.

facts.text: The eval harness replays past sittings per lane, per class — a read-only replay gated on DELIVERABLE-PRESENCE, not exit code. oc-ds exited 0 with no deliverable twice when sandbox-blocked — exit 0 proves nothing.

options: a lane can exit 0 with no deliverable

exercises.prompt: Why is the eval harness the #1 next layer?
options: it mechanizes the most-skipped layer (verification) and would've caught both defects

facts.text: Instrumented verification gates — a sitting won't close until exit + presence + class probe are recorded. Seam rule: gate logic stays a small script; past ~200 lines, stop and buy.

exercises.prompt: When does a sitting close under instrumented gates?
options: only after exit + presence + class probe are recorded
past ~200 lines of gate logic, stop and buy

exercises.prompt: The seam threshold in the blueprint is roughly:

facts.text: Skills compounding distills playbooks from the winning lanes' deliverable structure — but ONLY from ≥3 validated sittings per class. Wrong lessons compound too, which is why the eval harness is sequenced BEFORE it. The tightened rule: ≥3 validated sittings per class before distilling that class (6 same-day sittings is overfitting territory).

exercises.prompt: A playbook may be distilled only after:
Why is skills compounding sequenced AFTER the eval harness?

facts.text: Multica was REJECTED as an adoption on the license gate (1b forbids renaming/rebranding the UI without a written waiver — the owner's exact plan) and on the architecture gate (interactive board vs blind fanout; always-on = a re-platform trigger without a workload). The integration later landed in THIS workspace — label it owner-confirmed-current, not blueprint-derived.

options: reject as an adoption, on license AND architecture gates
adopt the tool, reject the ideas

exercises.prompt: What survived from the Multica evaluation?
The integration that later landed should be labeled:

facts.text: Re-platform triggers are workload-shaped, not maturity-shaped: concurrent mutation of the ledger, always-on / event-driven (a daemon, not cron), and trust-boundary crossing (multi-user, per-user auth). Nothing on the current roadmap approaches them — buy-verdict: nothing.

exercises.prompt: Which is a real re-platform trigger?

options: nothing — adopting now is re-platforming without a forcing trigger
